questions.q: What did Ginger think might have happened if she had had Black Beauty's bringing up?
choices: She might have had as good a temper as he had
She would have been trained to win races in London
She would have been sold to Squire Gordon much sooner
She would never have needed to be broken in at all
questions.evidence: I might have had as good a temper as you

questions.q: When was Ginger taken from her mother?
choices: As soon as she was weaned
When she was four years old
On the very day she was born
Just after she was broken in
questions.evidence: I was taken from my mother as soon as I was weaned

questions.q: What did the boys who passed through Ginger's field do?
choices: Threw stones to make the colts gallop
Fed the colts apples over the hedge
Rode the colts bareback around the field
Left the gate open so the colts got out
questions.evidence: the great boys passing through would fling stones to make us gallop

questions.q: How did the men first get the halter and bit on Ginger?
choices: They cornered her and forced her mouth open
They coaxed her gently with a sieve of oats
They waited until she was lying down asleep
They let her mother lead her into the stall first
questions.evidence: so by force they got on the halter and the bar into my mouth

questions.q: What kind of man was Samson, Mr. Ryder's son?
choices: Hard, with a hard voice, hard eye and hard hand
Gentle and patient, just like his old father
Shy, and rather afraid of the young horses
Kind enough, but careless and forgetful
questions.evidence: a hard voice, a hard eye, a hard hand

questions.q: What did Ginger believe Samson really wanted to do to her?
choices: Wear all the spirit out of her
Train her to win races at the fair
Make her his own favorite riding horse
Get her ready to sell to a kind family
questions.evidence: what he wanted was to wear all the spirit out of me

questions.q: What happened during the fight between Ginger and Samson on the training ground?
choices: She threw him off backward and galloped away
He tied her up in the stable and left her there
She broke through the gate and ran down the road
He gave up, got down and patted her neck

questions.q: What did Ginger have to put up with while standing alone in the hot field afterward?
choices: Flies, hunger, thirst and a tight saddle
Cold rain and a strong wind all afternoon
Dogs barking at her from across the hedge
Boys throwing stones at her over the fence
questions.evidence: the flies swarmed round me and settled on my bleeding flanks

questions.q: What did old Mr. Ryder bring when he came out to get Ginger at sunset?
choices: A sieve with oats in it
A long whip and a rope
A carrot and a red apple
A new bridle and a halter
questions.evidence: I saw the old master come out with a sieve in his hand

questions.q: What did old Mr. Ryder say to Samson about tempers?
choices: A bad-tempered man will never make a good-tempered horse
A vicious brute like Ginger needs a firmer hand every day
A horse must always be whipped if it will not obey at once
A hard day's work like that will settle any young horse
questions.evidence: a bad-tempered man will never make a good-tempered horse

questions.q: Why did Mr. Ryder have a bran mash made for Ginger?
choices: Her mouth was so sore she could not eat hay
She had grown too fat to be given oats
It was a treat to reward her for good work
She would not touch the grass in the field
questions.evidence: I could not eat the hay, the stalks hurt me

questions.q: What is the main idea of Ginger's story in this chapter?
choices: Force made her angry, but kindness took away her fear
Young horses should be kept shut in stables until broken
Training a horse is easy if the trainer is strong enough
Ginger was simply born with a bad and vicious temper
questions.evidence: his voice took all my fear away
